passages.note: Campaign issue page written in the third person ("Steve Hilton will"); the parent-trigger plan lists conversion to a charter as one option among several, chosen by parents, which shows a pro-charter side at most and not rung 5's conversion of failing schools to independent operators.
"New California Dream Charters" are county development charters for new cities, not charter schools.
Street-vending and restaurant sales-tax plan; mentions charter cities only, nothing on charter schools.

rows.reasoning: The only relevant passage is the campaign education page, written in the third person, whose parent-trigger plan says parents may trigger "administrative changes, curriculum overhauls, or conversion to a charter model"; conversion as one option among several, decided by parents, does not match rung 5 ("Convert failing district schools into charters run by independent operators") or say how readily a board should authorize charters. Even read as his own words it shows a pro-charter side only (direction-only); no passage separates the rungs.
needs_source: Steve Hilton's own first-person words (debate answer, questionnaire, interview) on how charter applications should be authorized or on converting failing schools to charters

quotes.text: If a school receives a D grade two years in a row, parents will have the right to trigger administrative changes, curriculum overhauls, or conversion to a charter model.
